The core duality emerges from two distinct behavioral objectives: injury prevention versus interference elimination. Fear drives avoidance (flee/hide), while aggression drives destruction (strike/eliminate). These behaviors are encoded in a shared threat perception kernel that varies with temperament. The mathematical structure reflects a dual-state dynamical system where each agent's behavior is determined by a latent temperament parameter and an objective threat signal. The system exhibits bifurcation points at high stimulus intensity, where temperament determines outcome. In GSI, this manifests as Bayesian classification of threat types; in GSE, as state-space transitions governed by temperament-weighted action kernels. Failure modes include misclassification of threat type or misalignment of temperament with environment.
